judged_text: In sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse applies the stripping minimum schema to the sync response, so parsedToken.data is {access_token, refresh_token: "refresh_token"} with no expires_in, and the code that follows persists that as the Zoom credential key. The stored Zoom credential loses its real refresh_token and expiry in sharing mode — expiry-based refresh logic misbehaves and the credential is bricked if sharing is ever turned off.

adjudication.rationale: In sharing mode, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` deliberately validates the refresh response against `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), and if `refresh_token` is missing it mutates the parsed data to `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`). Zoom’s refresh flow was changed from `zoomRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse(responseBody)` to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseBody, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema)` (`packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts`). That means in sharing mode the refresh response no longer needs to include a real refresh token, and the code path now produces a dummy refresh_token value, which is a correctness/data-integrity defect if the refreshed credential payload is persisted (as refresh flows typically do) because it can overwrite the real refresh token and break later non-sharing refresh behavior.
